correctness.rationale: For cut depths a,b,c>=0 and q=a²+b²+c² in (0,1/2), (a+b)²,(a+c)²,(b+c)²<=2q<1, so the three similar removed corner triangles have disjoint interiors. Thus area(K)=(1-q)/2. Edge-length/support-function formula V2(K,-K)=1/2 sum_F length(F)h_{-K}(unit outward normal) over the up-to-six edges simplifies to 1-s+ab+ac+bc with s=a+b+c. Therefore Δ=1-V2/(2 area K)=(2s-s²-q)/(2(1-q)). Fixed q gives a continuous interval sqrt(q)<=s<=sqrt(3q); derivative (1-s)/(1-q) is positive up to 1, negative after. The minimum is at one nonzero cut a=sqrt(q), giving sqrt(q)/(1+sqrt(q)); the maximum at equal cuts when q<=1/3, or at s=1 when q>=1/3, giving plateau Δ=1/2. Equality cases hold exactly by Cauchy–Schwarz and s-level feasibility. Independent convex-hull mixed-area calculations for five separate polygon choices matched exact identities within 3.4e-16. This is an exact 2D calculation, not extrapolation from numerical optimization.
residual_risks: Scope is the three side-parallel, nonoverlapping corner cuts of a single triangle, with q in (0,1/2), not arbitrary convex bodies or overlapping truncations.
